ordered_diagnoses: Prostatic stromal tumor of uncertain malignant potential

key_facts: 1 week of difficulty voiding
Urinary retention requiring catheterization
Prostate-specific antigen level was 0.62 ng/mL
Normal complete blood count, routine chemistries, and tumor markers
Digital rectal examination revealed an enlarged prostate
Palpable nodules and ill-defined border on prostate
Pelvic ultrasound confirmed a heterogeneous prostatic mass
Magnetic resonance imaging showed a 5.5-cm heterogeneous lesion
Cystoscopy raised suspicion for bladder invasion
Positron emission tomography–CT and colonoscopy suggested rectal invasion

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large prostatic mass, difficulty voiding, and urinary retention, along with imaging findings of a heterogeneous lesion and suspicion of bladder and rectal invasion, is more consistent with a sarcomatous process than a typical adenocarcinoma. The low PSA level also supports this diagnosis, as sarcomas often have lower PSA levels compared to adenocarcinomas.

rejected.label: Prostatic adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with elevated PSA levels and does not usually cause significant urinary obstruction at initial presentation

rejected.label: Prostate cancer
rejected.why: Too broad, as it encompasses multiple subtypes, including adenocarcinoma, which is less likely given the clinical presentation

rejected.label: Prostatic stromal tumor of uncertain malignant potential
rejected.why: While the biopsy result suggested this as a possibility, the aggressive clinical presentation and imaging findings are more suggestive of a malignant process like prostatic stromal sarcoma

rejected.label: Sarcomatoid carcinoma of the prostate
rejected.why: This entity is rare and typically presents with a history of prior adenocarcinoma or radiation therapy, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma of the prostate
rejected.why: While possible, the clinical and imaging findings are not specific enough to support this diagnosis over prostatic stromal sarcoma

rejected.label: Prostatic small cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms, elevated tumor markers, and a more aggressive clinical course, which is not seen in this case

rejected.label: Carcinosarcoma of the prostate
rejected.why: This is a rare tumor that contains both carcinomatous and sarcomatous elements, and the biopsy result did not suggest this specific diagnosis
